question: What is true about non-probability sampling when choosing who to study?

options.A: A computer selects names purely by random chance
options.B: Every person in the population must be listed
options.C: Sample sizes must always exceed one thousand
options.D: Not every member has an equal chance of selection

explanation: Non-probability sampling means participants are chosen deliberately rather than by random chance, so not everyone has an equal opportunity to be picked. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why might a researcher choose a non-probability sampling method?

options.A: To give every pregnant woman an equal selection chance
options.B: To prove exact statistics for the whole country
options.C: To eliminate all forms of human bias from the study
options.D: To study a very rare pregnancy complication easily

explanation: When conditions are rare or populations are hard to find, targeting specific accessible groups is the most practical way to gather information. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h1)

question: In which situation is non-probability sampling best to use?

options.A: Determining the precise national average weight of newborns
options.B: Exploring the emotional trauma of women who experienced stillbirth
options.C: Calculating the exact birth rate across all states in Nigeria
options.D: Testing a new malaria drug on a random national sample

explanation: Exploring sensitive or rare experiences relies on targeted, non-random participant selection rather than broad national surveys. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason for using non-probability sampling?

options.B: Achieving a statistically representative national census
options.C: Studying a population that is hidden or hard to reach
options.D: Working with very limited financial resources

explanation: Probability sampling is needed when the goal is a statistically representative census of an entire population. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h2)

question: What defines convenience sampling?

options.A: Choosing participants who are easiest to access
options.B: Handpicking experts based on strict qualifications
options.C: Asking participants to recruit their friends
options.D: Selecting names blindly from a hat

explanation: Convenience sampling involves simply taking whoever is available and willing to participate at the time and place of the study. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h3)

question: A student midwife interviews only traditional birth attendants with over twenty years of experience. What sampling method is this?
explanation: Choosing participants based on specific professional traits or experience levels is known as purposive sampling. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does snowball sampling help find new study participants?

options.A: By setting up desks at market entrances
options.B: Through referrals made by current participants
options.D: By pulling hospital folder numbers randomly

explanation: Snowball sampling uses existing study subjects to connect with and recruit other eligible people from their social networks. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h4)

question: When is quota sampling most useful in a hospital study?

options.A: When there are no records of patients available anywhere
options.B: When you only have time to interview the very first patient who arrives
options.C: When you want every patient in the ward to have an equal chance
options.D: When you need a fixed number of participants from specific categories

explanation: Quota sampling sets numerical targets for different subgroups to ensure they are adequately represented in the final sample. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is a major limitation of non-probability sampling?

options.A: It is impossible to conduct interviews with the participants
options.B: Ethical boards automatically reject all non-random studies
options.C: Results cannot be safely generalized to the wider population
options.D: It requires massive financial budgets and computer software

explanation: Because participants are not chosen randomly, the findings apply only to the specific group studied rather than the general public. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h5)

question: What primary type of bias is most common in non-probability sampling?
explanation: Selection bias happens naturally when researchers choose participants based on convenience or personal judgment rather than random chance. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h5)
